3.name: Rosa explains the desk had been disturbed
3.description: Rosa tells Asha she knew someone had been in the desk before her but did not know who.
evidence: Rosa looked at Asha very steadily. "I knew that someone had been in the desk before me. I did not know who."

3.name: Rosa suspects funeral home workers
3.description: Rosa says she thought the funeral home staff might have been the ones in the room, citing their early arrival and the younger worker's time alone in the hallway.
evidence: "I thought it might be the funeral home — they had come for the body at four in the morning and one of them, the younger one, had been alone in the hallway for several minutes while I was downstairs."

3.name: Rosa fears a child entered the room
3.description: Rosa admits she feared one of the matriarch's children had come into the room while she was downstairs.
evidence: "That one of her children had come into the room while I was downstairs."

3.name: Asha senses Daniel's attention
3.description: Asha avoids looking at Daniel but feels the intensity of his attention in the quiet hallway.
evidence: The hallway behind them was very quiet.
Asha did not turn to look at Daniel. She did not need to. She could feel the temperature of his attention the way a person feels a radiator coming on in a cold room.

3.name: Asha thanks Rosa
3.description: Asha acknowledges Rosa's information and the conversation moves on.
evidence: "Thank you, Rosa."
They went on.

3.name: They search the third-floor office
3.description: Asha and Rosa continue to the third floor, where an old office remains mostly intact despite the matriarch's inability to climb there for years.
evidence: They went on. The third floor, where the matriarch had not climbed in eight years on account of her knee but where a small office had once been kept and had been left more or less intact.

3.name: Rosa opens the filing cabinet
3.description: Rosa opens a filing cabinet in the old office to inspect its contents.
evidence: Rosa opened a filing cabinet.

3.name: Asha finds old records in the cabinet
3.description: Asha sees that the cabinet contains outdated folders and records, including tax returns, warranty cards, and Daniel's school report cards.
evidence: Inside were folders, manila and green both, none of them recent.
Tax returns from the nineteen-nineties.
A binder of warranty cards for appliances long since replaced.
A folder of school report cards for Daniel from 1979 through 1985

3.name: Daniel reacts to the report cards
3.description: Asha senses Daniel's deep exhale as Rosa lifts aside his school report cards, suggesting he fears they might be read aloud.
evidence: which Asha glimpsed only briefly as Rosa lifted it aside
which she thought afterward might have been the moment when Daniel exhaled most deeply, as if he had been afraid Rosa was going to take that folder out of the cabinet and read aloud from it.

3.name: They fail to find a codicil
3.description: The search of the cabinet turns up no green folder containing anything like the codicil they are looking for.
evidence: There were no green folders containing anything resembling a codicil.

3.name: finds no codicil in cabinet
3.description: The search turns up no green folder or codicil in the cabinet, disappointing the group.
evidence: There were no green folders containing anything resembling a codicil.

3.name: group returns to front hall
3.description: The four people come back downstairs and gather in the front hall after the unsuccessful search.
evidence: They came back down the stairs. The four of them stood in the front hall

3.name: Daniel presses for answer
3.description: Daniel pauses at the newel post and prompts the others with a terse 'Well,' signaling impatience.
evidence:
Daniel had his hand on the newel post.

"Well," he said.

3.name: Asha reports no codicil found
3.description: Asha states that there is no codicil in the house so far and that she will continue searching.
evidence: "There's no codicil."
"There's no codicil *here.*"

"It means," Asha said, "that there is no codicil here. It does not mean there is no codicil. It means I have not found it in the places one would expect to find it. It means I am going to keep looking."

3.name: Daniel refuses prolonged search
3.description: Daniel objects that he has buyers, a written offer, taxes due, and an unpaid roofer, and says he cannot keep the house in limbo while Asha searches.
evidence: "Counselor." He said the word with a flatness that was not quite contempt but was not quite anything else either. "I have buyers. I have an offer in writing as of yesterday afternoon. I have property taxes due at the end of next month and I have a roofer who has called me three times about a repair my mother authorized in November and never paid for. I cannot keep this house in stasis while you turn over every cushion in the building looking for a piece of paper that no one in this room has actually seen."

3.name: Asha cites Rosa's sighting
3.description: When Daniel dismisses the codicil, Asha insists that Rosa has seen it before.
evidence: "Rosa has seen it."
"Rosa says she has seen it."

3.name: Rosa remains unshaken
3.description: Rosa does not react to the accusation or skepticism, and Asha notes her resilience.
evidence: The sentence sat in the hallway. Rosa did not flinch. She had been called worse things in her life, Asha thought, by people

3.name: Daniel distinguishes Rosa's testimony
3.description: Daniel insists that Rosa merely says she saw the room, framing her account as testimony rather than direct proof.
evidence: "Rosa has seen it."
"Rosa says she has seen it."

3.name: Asha judges Daniel's wording
3.description: Asha internally recognizes Daniel's phrasing as a way of reducing Rosa to a category rather than treating her as an equal witness.
evidence: Rosa did not flinch.
there was something in the way Daniel had pitched the word — *says* — that had nothing to do with disagreement and everything to do with reducing her to a category.

3.name: Lucia rebukes Daniel
3.description: Lucia finally speaks up and tells Daniel not to treat Rosa that way, especially not in front of others.
evidence: Lucia spoke for the first time since they had come down the stairs.
"Daniel."
"Don't."
"Don't do that. Don't do that to her. Not in front of —"

3.name: Lucia rejects conditional respect
3.description: Lucia stops herself from saying 'strangers' and insists Daniel should not do this at all, regardless of who is present.
evidence: She did not say *not in front of strangers,* because Asha was a stranger and Marcus was a stranger and Lucia perhaps did not want to imply that the not-doing was conditional on strangers being absent.
"Don't do it at all."

3.name: Daniel defends his statement as legal truth
3.description: Daniel denies wrongdoing and argues that he is only stating the legally correct distinction between a witness and a document.
evidence: "I'm not doing anything. I'm saying what is legally true. Rosa is a witness. A witness's testimony is not the same as a document."

3.name: Daniel seeks legal confirmation
3.description: Daniel appeals to the counselor to confirm his legal distinction and receives agreement.
evidence: "Counselor — you'll back me up on this — a witness who saw a document being prepared is not the same as a document. Yes?"
"That is correct as far as it goes."

3.name: Daniel claims he only meant the legal point
3.description: After the counselor agrees, Daniel asserts that this legal distinction is all he was saying.
evidence: "There. That is all I am saying."

3.name: Lucia challenges Daniel's tone
3.description: Lucia tells Daniel that his wording carried a different, more insulting meaning than the legal point he claims.
evidence: "You said it differently than that," Lucia said quietly.

3.name: Lucia accuses Daniel of patronizing Rosa
3.description: Lucia explains that Daniel's phrasing echoed how he used to dismiss their mother, implying he was treating Rosa as someone to be brushed aside.
evidence: "You said *Rosa says.* You said it the way you used to say *Mami says* when we were children and you didn't want to do something she had asked you to do."

3.name: Lucia begins a sharper accusation
3.description: Lucia starts to say that Daniel spoke as if Rosa were something lesser, escalating the confrontation.
evidence: "You said it like she was

3.name: Lucia accuses Daniel of dismissing Rosa
3.description: Lucia tells Daniel he repeated Rosa's words in a way that made her opinion seem unimportant, comparing it to how he used to evade their mother as children.
evidence: "You said *Rosa says.* You said it the way you used to say *Mami says* when we were children and you didn't want to do something she had asked you to do. You said it like she was — like her saying didn't count."

3.name: Daniel denies Lucia's accusation
3.description: Daniel rejects Lucia's claim that he dismissed Rosa's authority.
evidence: "I did not."

3.name: Lucia insists Daniel is lying
3.description: Lucia flatly contradicts Daniel and refuses to back down.
evidence: "You did."

3.name: siblings argue in the hallway
3.description: Daniel and Lucia face each other in the mother's front hall, revealing a long-standing sibling conflict that Asha recognizes as familiar and habitual.
evidence: "They were facing each other now, brother and sister, in the front hall of the house their mother had lived in for fifty-one years"
"she had the brief disorienting sense that she had ceased to be in the room"
"they had probably been doing in this hallway since they were eight and twelve."

3.name: Asha reasserts control over the exchange
3.description: Asha interrupts the siblings, identifies them formally, and instructs them to answer her question separately without interrupting each other.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano," she said. "Ms. Serrano."
"I am going to ask the two of you a question, and I am going to ask you to answer it separately, and not to interrupt each other. Is that all right."

3.name: siblings agree to answer separately
3.description: Daniel and Lucia each consent to Asha's instruction to answer her question separately.
evidence: "Daniel said, \"Fine.\""
"Lucia said, \"Yes.\""

3.name: Asha questions Daniel about removed documents
3.description: Asha asks Daniel whether he took any documents or papers from the house or sewing-room desk after his mother's death without telling anyone.
evidence: "Mr. Serrano. Did you, at any point between your mother's death and this morning, remove any item — any document, any folder, any piece of paper — from this house, from the sewing-room desk, or from any other location, without telling me or Rosa or your sister."
3.time_hint: between your mother's death and this morning

3.name: Daniel is caught off guard by the accusation
3.description: Daniel reacts silently and realizes the question is being asked bluntly in front of the others, showing he did not expect this confrontation.
evidence: "He looked at her."
"He had not expected the question to be put quite that way, that bluntly, in the front hall, with his sister and his mother's housekeeper and his attorney's paralegal all standing within"

3.name: Daniel denies taking anything
3.description: Daniel answers bluntly that he has not taken anything from the house.
evidence: "No," he said.

3.name: Asha asks Lucia the same question
3.description: Asha repeats the accusation to Lucia, pressing her for the same answer in front of the others.
evidence: "Thank you. Ms. Serrano. Same question."

3.name: Lucia hesitates before answering
3.description: Lucia pauses and weighs her response before speaking, revealing her internal conflict.
evidence: Lucia hesitated.
She hesitated for perhaps two seconds, which was not long in absolute terms but was very long in the terms of the front hall of that house at that moment

3.name: Lucia denies removing anything
3.description: Lucia states that she has not taken anything out of the house.
evidence: "I have not taken anything out of this house," Lucia said.

3.name: Lucia reveals finding a hidden letter
3.description: Lucia admits she found a letter hidden in the sewing room after the funeral.
evidence: "I found a letter. In the sewing room. The day after the funeral. It was not in the desk. It was — it was tucked into the pincushion. The big velvet one she kept on the machine."

3.name: Lucia keeps the letter in her bag upstairs
3.description: Lucia explains that she did not remove the letter from the house and that it is currently in her bag upstairs.
evidence: "I did not take it out of the house. It is in the house. It is in my bag upstairs."

3.name: Daniel reacts in confusion
3.description: Daniel responds in shock and confusion to Lucia's revelation about the letter.
evidence: Daniel said, "What."

3.name: Lucia withholds eye contact from Daniel
3.description: Lucia avoids looking at Daniel and continues addressing Asha instead, signaling tension between them.
evidence: Lucia did not look at him. She kept looking at Asha.

3.name: Lucia identifies the letter as a personal message
3.description: Lucia explains that the letter is from her mother and is addressed to her, her brother, and Rosa.
evidence: "It is — it is not the will. It is not a codicil. It is a letter from my mother. It is addressed to me and to my brother and to Rosa."

3.name: Lucia admits rereading the letter nightly
3.description: Lucia confesses that she has read the letter repeatedly since finding it and has been unsure whether to turn it over.
evidence: "I read it the night I found it and I have read it again every night since and I did not know whether to give it to you because I did not know whether you would think it was evidence of something or ju
3.time_hint: the night I found it / every night since

3.name: Lucia reveals she kept the letter
3.description: Lucia explains that she found the letter, has reread it every night, and hesitated to give it to Daniel because she did not know whether it was evidence or just a letter.
evidence: "I read it the night I found it and I have read it again every night since and I did not know whether to give it to you because I did not know whether you would think it was evidence of something or just — a letter."

3.name: Daniel reacts with alarm
3.description: Daniel addresses Lucia by name and his voice becomes very thin, signaling distress at her revelation.
evidence: "Lucia," Daniel said. His voice had gone very thin.

3.name: Lucia apologizes for withholding the letter
3.description: Lucia apologizes repeatedly and admits she has not known what to do about the letter.
evidence: "I'm sorry. I'm sorry, Daniel. I have not known what to do."

3.name: Daniel confronts Lucia about the delay
3.description: Daniel points out that Lucia has had the letter for nearly a week and never told him or anyone else.
evidence: "You have had it for a *week.*"
"I have had it for six days."
"And you didn't tell me."
"No."
"You didn't tell *anyone*."
"I'm telling someone now."

3.name: Asha notices Daniel's wedding ring
3.description: Asha observes Daniel gripping and releasing the newel post and notices his wedding ring, prompting thoughts about his unseen wife and the week's events in the house.
evidence: "Asha watched Daniel's hand tighten on the newel post and then loosen."

"He had a wedding ring on, she noticed, and the ring caught the light when his hand moved, and she thought briefly and irrelevantly about the wife she had not yet met and wondered what that woman knew about what was happening in this house this week."

3.name: Asha sends Lucia to retrieve the letter
3.description: Asha instructs Lucia to go upstairs and get the letter, and Lucia complies.
evidence: "Ms. Serrano," she said. "Would you go and get the letter, please."
"Lucia nodded and went up the stairs."

3.name: Daniel remains tense as Lucia leaves
3.description: Daniel watches Lucia go upstairs without moving from the newel post, while Rosa stands silently by the dining room door observing the moment.
evidence: "Daniel watched her go and did not move from the newel post."

"Rosa stood very still by the door to the dining room, with her arms folded across her cardigan, and her face had taken on the expression of a person who has been waiting a long time for a thing she was not entirely sure would happen, and was now watching it happen."

3.name: Daniel asks for a private word
3.description: While Lucia is still on the stairs, Daniel quietly asks Asha for a word, indicating he wants to speak before the letter is produced.
evidence: "Counselor," Daniel said quietly, while Lucia was still on the stairs. "A word."

3.name: Asha refuses Daniel's request
3.description: Asha insists that any private conversation must wait until after they see the letter, and Daniel silently challenges her with a look.
evidence: "After we see the letter."
"Before."
"After."
"He looked at her. She looked back."

3.name: Asha delays discussion until after the letter
3.description: Asha insists they discuss matters only after seeing the letter, while the other speaker presses to talk first.
evidence: "A word."
"After we see the letter."
"Before."
"After."

3.name: Asha withholds emotional reaction
3.description: Asha maintains a controlled, unreadable expression, signaling restraint and self-possession.
evidence: She kept her face exactly as she had kept it during the inventory of the drawers, exactly as she had kept it when Rosa had said *the green folder,* exactly as she had kept it the first time she had walked into this house six days ago

3.name: Asha recognizes Daniel's restraint limit
3.description: Asha observes that Daniel stops pressing her because he is close to becoming the kind of person he is trying not to seem like.
evidence: He did not push.
he had reached, she suspected, the limit of what he could push without becoming the thing he was working very hard not to appear to be.

3.name: Lucia returns with envelope
3.description: Lucia comes back down the stairs carrying a tote bag and produces a plain envelope from it.
evidence: Lucia came back down the stairs.
She had a canvas tote bag over her shoulder
she set it on the small table beneath the hall mirror and reached into it and took out an envelope.

3.name: Lucia reveals letter hidden in pincushion
3.description: Lucia explains that the letter was hidden inside an envelope, which had been concealed in the pincushion.
evidence: "Inside the envelope," Lucia said, "is the letter. The envelope was inside the pincushion. The letter was inside the envelope."

3.name: Asha takes envelope
3.description: Asha asks permission and receives the envelope from Lucia without opening it immediately.
evidence: "May I."
"Yes."
Asha took it.
She did not open it in the hall.

3.name: Asha moves meeting to dining room
3.description: Asha decides they should sit down and continue in the dining room before opening the letter.
evidence: "Let's sit down. The dining room, please."

3.name: Group sits at dining table
3.description: They enter the dining room and take seats, with Daniel occupying the head of the table by default.
evidence: They went into the dining room and sat.
Daniel at the head of the table, because no one had told him not to

3.name: refuse to open envelope in hall
3.description: Asha chooses not to open the envelope in the hallway and instead moves the group to sit down.
evidence: She did not open it in the hall.
She said, "Let's sit down. The dining room, please."

3.name: gather in dining room
3.description: The group goes into the dining room and takes their seats for the reading.
evidence: They went into the dining room and sat.

3.name: Daniel sits at head of table
3.description: Daniel takes the head seat, reflecting his long-standing place in the house.
evidence: Daniel at the head of the table, because no one had told him not to and because he had been sitting there at every meal in this house since he was nine years old.

3.name: Rosa sits at table
3.description: Rosa sits in a chair at the table after Asha gestures for her to do so, marking an unusual but meaningful change in her behavior.
evidence: Rosa to his right, which was not where Rosa would normally have sat — Rosa would normally have been standing somewhere in the kitchen doorway — but Asha gestured to the chair and Rosa sat in it without comment, and Asha thought that the sitting was itself a kind of testimony.

3.name: Marcus takes wall chair with box and camera
3.description: Marcus positions himself by the wall with his banker's box and camera, indicating he is documenting or preserving the proceedings.
evidence: Marcus took a chair by the wall, his banker's box on the floor at his feet, his camera in his lap.

3.name: Asha dons gloves and opens envelope
3.description: Asha puts on cotton gloves and opens the envelope containing the letter.
evidence: Asha put on the cotton gloves again.
She opened the envelope.

3.name: Asha examines letter
3.description: Asha inspects the letter's physical appearance and handwriting before reading it.
evidence: Inside was a single sheet of cream-colored stationery, folded in thirds, written on both sides in a hand that was small and slanted and disciplined, the handwriting of a woman who had been taught penmanship in a Catholic school in San Juan in the late nineteen-forties and had never seen any reason to write any other way.

3.name: Asha rereads letter silently
3.description: Asha reads the letter twice to herself before speaking aloud.
evidence: She read it once silently.
She read it again silently.

3.name: Asha announces aloud reading
3.description: Asha tells Ms. Serrano she will read the letter aloud and gives her a chance to stop the reading.
evidence: Then she said, "I am going to read this aloud. Ms. Serrano, please tell me if at any point you would prefer me to stop."
"I won't."
"All right."

3.name: Asha begins reading letter
3.description: Asha starts reading the letter aloud, beginning with an intimate address to her children and Rosa.
evidence: She read.
*Mis hijos, y Rosa, who is also mine —*
